housing.summary: Waterford city centre 1-bedroom apartments listed at approximately EUR 1,300 per month on Daft.ie. Deposit norm is typically one month but up to two months under Irish RPZ rules. Daft.ie is the main local rental portal.

banking.summary: To open a bank account in Ireland, newcomers need photo ID (passport), proof of address (utility bill or tenancy agreement dated within 3 months), and PPS number if employed. AIB and Bank of Ireland both operate in Waterford.
required_docs: Proof of address (utility bill or tenancy agreement dated within 3 months)

schools.summary: Waterford has no IB or French international school listed on the Department of Education school finder. The main schools directory for Ireland is available via the Department of Education. Most international families use the Irish national curriculum schools.

legal_admin.summary: Non-EU expats staying more than 90 days must register with Immigration Service Delivery (ISD) within 90 days of arrival to obtain an Irish Residence Permit (IRP). Registration is done via the ISD online customer portal booking system. Fee is EUR 300.
legal_admin.registration_step: Book an appointment via the ISD online customer portal at irishimmigration.ie; attend with passport, permission letter and supporting documents; pay EUR 300 fee; receive IRP card by post.

tax_finance.summary: A PPS (Personal Public Service) number is obtained by applying online via MyWelfare.ie (if you have a MyGovID account) or by booking an in-person appointment at your local Intreo centre or DSP office. You need photo ID and proof of address.

transport.summary: Waterford is served by Bus Eireann city bus services. The adult monthly TFI Leap Card pass for the Waterford City Red Zone is EUR 54. Non-EU licence holders must apply to NDLS to exchange; EU/EEA licences can be exchanged directly at NDLS. Newcomers ordinarily resident in Ireland register with a local GP practice directly; medical card can be applied for via HSE for full eligibility.
transport.driving_licence_exchange: EU/EEA licence holders can exchange for an Irish licence at any NDLS centre (fee EUR 65); non-EU licence holders from recognised states may also exchange; others must pass Irish driving test. Apply at ndls.ie.
transport.healthcare_registration: Contact a local GP practice directly to register as a patient. To apply for a medical card (free GP services), apply via mywelfare.ie or HSE. Ordinary residence (1 year intent) required for full HSE entitlement.
